critical_changes: Disclose in Section 4.5 (and briefly in the abstract/Section 1) that the pre-collection protocol designated D as the only ranking criterion ('Rank models only on D'). The alignment-ratio ranking featured in the abstract (GPT Image 2 aligns best in all three representations) was adopted after collection, once D's rankings proved representation-dependent. Its values, resampled 'best' shares and recognition Spearman correlations were already known when the plan that fixed them was written (painter_tmlr_diagnostics_v5 PLAN). Reword 'each fixed before its outcomes were computed' so it does not imply protection for these quantities. Editing only.

Correct the sign error in Appendix A (Repeat dependence, p. 18). '(-3.4 to -0.7% change in squared prediction error relative to zero)' reports predictive gains, (MSE_zero - MSE_held)/MSE_zero, as error changes. The held-out squared error was 0.7-3.4% higher, not lower. Write '+0.7 to +3.4% change in squared prediction error' or 'predictive gain of -3.4 to -0.7%', and update the drift_gain registry entry.
minor_changes: Describe the alignment ratio as the alignment of scene-wise differences with the pooled pattern. Because Q = B/H + V_scene, it treats scene-specific variation as misalignment. Report the scene-averaged beta/sqrt(B/H) as well: GPT Image 2 stays best in all representations, but Nano Banana 2 moves from last to third in the 31 features.
Section 5.3: note that D_held is approximately 1 - (beta/sqrt(Q))^2 (e.g. 0.551 vs 0.554 for GPT Image 2), so its agreement with the alignment ratio is not independent corroboration.

Section 1 bullet 3: qualify GPT Image 1's D > 1 as Section 5.3 does (unadjusted interval; Bonferroni-over-six interval [0.935, 2.210] includes 1; reverses at repeat correlation 0.22), or restrict the statement to Flare and Sunburst.
Section 5.3 p. 11: narrow 'Content does not explain the difference' to 'title-derived content-class targets on the 11 non-mixed scenes change embedding errors by at most 0.037'.
State n = 6 wherever Spearman correlations are quoted (0.94, 0.89, 0.60-0.77, -0.14 to 0.66); one adjacent swap moves rho by 0.057. Preferably add resampling intervals.

Appendix A 'Model selection': temper 'argue that the six requested configurations reached different generators' to 'produced distinguishable output distributions'. Cost and distance differences do not establish distinct checkpoints.
Section 6: the condition for the shared term to dominate is beta < 4S/H. Rephrase 'unless the model exaggerates the reference differences (beta > 1)' to say that beta <= 1 suffices.
Report that 4 of 653 eligible reference works (2 Monet, 1 Pissarro, 1 Cezanne) failed feature extraction, so 649 is after exclusion.
Add uncertainty (scene-resampling or binomial intervals) to the recognition accuracies in Table 3.
Commit to depositing the 1,008 generated images upon de-anonymisation so features can be re-extracted from pixels.

Reduce number density in Sections 5.3-5.5 by moving secondary ranges to the appendix tables. State early in Section 5.1 that the comparison with the exact-differences benchmark reduces to B/H versus 1.
Supplement: have the claim registry record sign/units, so that the replay check can catch semantic errors like the drift sign.
factual_errors: Appendix A, Repeat dependence (p. 18): '(-3.4 to -0.7% change in squared prediction error relative to zero)'. The source values are predictive gains, (MSE_zero - MSE_held)/MSE_zero = -3.38% to -0.72% (reports/painter_request_timing_v1). The squared prediction error increased by 0.7-3.4%. As worded, the parenthetical contradicts 'predicts those differences worse than no drift'.
